# Postgres to Apache Doris

[Apache Doris](https://doris.apache.org/) is a columnar analytical database that speaks the MySQL
protocol. Since version 4.1 it can follow Postgres, without Kafka or Debezium.
A single `CREATE JOB` statement creates the target tables, copies the existing rows, and then
streams changes from a replication slot on the source. This is the statement the lab ran:

```sql
CREATE JOB pg_mirror_job
PROPERTIES ("max_interval" = "1")
ON STREAMING
FROM POSTGRES (
    "jdbc_url" = "jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/app",
    "driver_url" = "https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/postgresql/postgresql/42.7.4/postgresql-42.7.4.jar",
    "driver_class" = "org.postgresql.Driver",
    "user" = "app", "password" = "...",
    "database" = "app", "schema" = "doris_src",
    "include_tables" = "docs",
    "offset" = "initial"
)
TO DATABASE pg_mirror ("table.create.properties.replication_num" = "1");
```

## Replication latency and schema changes

The lab runs one Doris frontend and one backend next to pg16 and points a job at the project's
tables. On Doris 4.1.4 the job behaved like this:

| | |
|---|---|
| source side | the job creates its own publication and slot, one per job, and `DROP JOB` removes both |
| latency | about 11 s with the default `max_interval` of 10, and about 5 s with 1 |
| types | `jsonb` lands as `text`, `uuid` as `text`, `timestamptz` as `datetime(6)` in the Doris time zone |
| `vector` | auto table creation refuses it, and in a pre-created table it arrives as NULL without an error |
| generated columns | copied by the snapshot, then dropped once streaming starts |
| DDL | added and dropped columns propagate |

Compared with [logical replication](logical-replication.qmd), changes take seconds to arrive
instead of milliseconds, while schema changes on the source come across on their own instead of
stopping the stream.

## Vector columns

Doris reads the change stream through Debezium's Postgres connector, which has no converter for
pgvector's `vector` type, so the column arrives as NULL without any error. The
[Doris CDC notebook](../notebooks/doris_cdc.ipynb) verifies a workaround, in which a trigger on the
source keeps a `real[]` copy of each embedding. The copy arrives as `ARRAY<FLOAT>`, and Doris's own
`cosine_distance` then returns the same top five results as pgvector.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Resource requirements

The Doris images are large (4 GB for the frontend, 9 GB for the backend), and their defaults assume
a dedicated machine, with an 8 GB heap and a backend sized to 90% of memory. On Docker Desktop that
ends in `MEM_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, so the lab's compose file caps both (`DORIS_FE_HEAP`, `DORIS_BE_MEM`)
to fit beside the other containers.
:::
